noah: Quick note — hitting inconsistent retry/timeouts in the Kotlin SDK sample on some devices. Behavior: when multiple concurrent requests get 401, our interceptor refreshes token but a few callers time out and the connection becomes unusable afterward.

emma: What timeout are you using? OkHttp call timeout or read timeout?

noah: callTimeout=25s, read/connect default. Sequence: request gets 401, interceptor suspends to refresh token (~2s), meanwhile other parallel requests also 401 and wait. If some callers exceed callTimeout while waiting, OkHttp cancels and we see SocketException later.

raj: This sounds like the Authenticator vs Interceptor race. Authenticator runs on OkHttp internal threads and can trigger multiple refresh attempts. We recommend moving refresh into an app-level interceptor with a single-flight Mutex to ensure one refresh at a time.

emma: Also consider lowering parallelism with Dispatcher.setMaxRequestsPerHost(6) to avoid huge bursts during refresh.

noah: I toggled to interceptor + Mutex and added a retry-once after refresh. That removed duplicates but still a few "stream allocation still active" warnings on Android 11 emulator. Adding response.body?.close() before retry helped.

raj: For sample app we should document: 1) prefer interceptor-managed refresh with coroutine Mutex; 2) always close response bodies in failure paths; 3) avoid call.clone() for retries if the original call might be canceled — use client.newCall(newRequest) instead.

emma: I'll update the Android guide with code snippets and a tiny repro script (Pixel 3A/Android 11 emulator, run 6 concurrent POSTs to /v1/complete, stub auth delay).
